sections.heading: C - New York Driver Manual Chapter Five: Intersections and turns
sections.markdown:
## C - New York Driver Manual Chapter Five: Intersections and turns

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
Most crashes strike at intersections and in big parking lots during turns, and right-of-way rules settle conflicts that signs and greens leave open, such as a left turner facing straight-through traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=34]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
Approaching drivers yield to traffic already inside, so a green-straight driver waits out a left turner mid-intersection before entering. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=34]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Simultaneous opposite arrivals give straight and right movements priority over left turns, with left turners entering on green only when nobody ahead also turns left, holding right of center with straight wheels, finishing when oncoming clears, yielding the same way into driveways and lots, and waiting out any doubtful gap. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=34]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
At uncontrolled or simultaneous-stop right-angle corners, the left driver yields to the right driver, even going straight against straight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=34]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A01
Driveway, lot and private-road exits must stop and yield to roadway traffic and pedestrians, watching left for right exits, both ways for left exits, and any crossing pedestrian. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=34]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A01
Drivers yield to lawful crosswalk pedestrians marked or not, slowing or stopping as needed and guarding cyclists too, waiting out red-light pedestrians after green and crosswalk users on either side before turning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=34]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A02
Never enter on a green you cannot clear, waiting out backed-up far sides and offset cross-streets instead of gridlocking the box. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A02
Motorists entering a traffic circle or rotary must give way to vehicles already circulating inside, while detailed roundabout navigation appears in Chapter Eight [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A02
Fire, ambulance, police and authorized emergency responders showing red, red-blue or red-white flashes with possible sirens or air-horns, which police may skip, command an immediate safe pull to the right edge and stop from every direction, after clearing any intersection, including opposite-lane two-way approaches and sirens of unknown location. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A02
Lit-and-sounding emergency drivers may legally speed, run reds and stop or yield signs, reverse one-way streets and invent turning moves, so nearby drivers stay extra cautious despite the responder's duty of care. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A02
The Move Over law demands care, reduced speed and, on multilane parkways, interstates and controlled roads, a lane shift away from shoulder-stopped emergency and hazard vehicles flashing emergency, amber or blue-green lights unless unsafe, plus blue-green-light vehicles and any shoulder-parked vehicle on parkways and controlled highways, all punishable as a moving violation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A02
Volunteer firefighters show blue, volunteer ambulance crews green, and plows, tow rigs, tow-blue combos, rural mail carriers and school buses amber, yet none count as authorized emergency vehicles, their drivers obey every law, and others yield only by courtesy. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=35]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A03
Every turn and lane change needs lamp or hand signals at least one hundred feet ahead, preferably before braking, with illustrated hand shapes on the page. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=36]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A03
Turn preparation slows down, scans all sides with motorcycle paranoia since unseen bikes cause most car-bike crashes, holds wheels straight until committed, tracks the tighter rear-wheel path, and guards pedestrians, cyclists, moped riders and low-hidden wheelchair, stroller and suitcase users, especially turning right. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=36]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A03
Right turns hug the right edge without sweeping wide and land in the entered road's right lane unless signs say otherwise. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=36]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A03
One-way-to-one-way lefts stage in the left lane and land in the entered road's left lane where two exist. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=36]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A03
One-way-to-two-way lefts stage left and enter right of center hugging the line, watching left-road traffic and hard-to-judge motorcycles. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=36]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A04
Two-way-to-two-way lefts stage in the right half near center, favor the intersection's left side to clear opposing left turners, enter right of center hugging the line, and watch oncoming, cross-lane and easily-missed motorcycle traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A04
Two-way-to-one-way lefts stage in the right half near center, cut before the intersection's middle, and land in the entered left lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A04
Two-way-to-four-lane lefts stage in the right half near center, enter the left lane right of center, and drift outward when traffic allows. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A04
U-turns reverse direction, belong in lots and driveways with forward re-entry rather than on highways, start only from the leftmost pavement near the centerline never the right lane, and need green-arrow permission with yielding where allowed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A04
U-turns are illegal where other drivers cannot see your vehicle from five hundred feet in either direction, in New York City business districts, at NO U-TURN signs, on limited-access expressways even where paths connect the sides, and in school zones, whereas a three-point turn may be used on a narrow two-way street unless prohibited and may be required on your road test [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=37]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A05
Three-point turns run right-signal pull-over and stop, left-signal all-direction check, left sweep to the far curb, full-right back-up with a rear watch stopping shy of the curb, then full-left forward exit when safe. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=38]
